name: Executive Office (CEO Office)
dlc: Further Adventures in Finance and Felony
income: Unlocks CEO work, VIP Work and Special Cargo; the office computer is used to buy warehouses and run cargo missions.
description: The headquarters for a SecuroServ CEO, available in four towers around the city. It is the gateway to Special Cargo and Vehicle Cargo businesses and can be decorated and expanded with garages.

earnings.perHourNote: The office itself earns nothing; its value comes from the Special Cargo and Vehicle Warehouse businesses it unlocks.

pros: Required gateway to crate and vehicle cargo businesses
Relatively cheap entry point at the base tier
Can be expanded with office garages and a vehicle workshop
cons: Generates no income on its own
Upgrades and decor add a lot to the price without boosting earnings
verdict: Worth buying the cheapest one, since it is the key to two solid CEO businesses; the expensive towers add nothing but looks.

name: Special Cargo Warehouse
dlc: Further Adventures in Finance and Felony
requires: Own an Executive Office and be a CEO
income: Source crates through buy missions, store them, then sell in bulk; bigger sales pay more per crate.
description: Storage for crates of contraband sourced by a CEO. Warehouses come in small (16 crates), medium (42) and large (111) sizes, and up to five can be owned.

earnings.perHourNote: Middle of guide estimates (about $150K-$226K/hr) for sourcing and selling a full large warehouse; a full 111-crate sale is about $2.22M against roughly $666K in crate costs.

pros: A full large-warehouse sale is one of the biggest single paydays in the game
Sourcing missions are short and can be done alone
Small warehouses are very cheap
cons: Sourcing a large warehouse takes many hours of repetitive missions
Big sales can roll multiple delivery vehicles, which is risky solo
Crates must be bought, so there is an upfront cost per run
verdict: A decent active grind if you buy the large warehouse and sell in one go, but slower and more tedious than newer options.

name: Vehicle Warehouse
requires: Own an Executive Office and be a CEO
income: Steal high-end cars, store them and export them to buyers; condition on delivery affects the payout.
description: An underground warehouse for stolen high-end vehicles, run as part of the Import/Export business. Only one can be owned, and filling collections unlocks bonus vehicles for Special Vehicle Work.

earnings.perHourNote: Middle of widely varying estimates ($150K to $400K/hr) for stealing and exporting Top Range cars at about $80K net each; repairs and cooldowns lower the real figure.

pros: Top Range exports pay around $80K each
Each steal and sale is quick and handled with one car
Good use of the CEO Office alongside crates
cons: Damage on delivery cuts the payout
Sale cooldowns limit how fast you can cash out
Needs a full warehouse for the best car mix
verdict: Solid solo money for players who enjoy driving, but sale cooldowns and damage penalties keep it below the top earners.

name: MC Clubhouse
income: Unlocks Clubhouse Contracts and MC work for a Motorcycle Club President, and is required for the MC drug and forgery businesses.
description: A biker hangout that lets the owner found a Motorcycle Club. It includes a bar, a garage and a custom bike shop, and serves as the base for the MC businesses.

earnings.perHourNote: No reliable hourly figure; the bar earns small sums from resupplies and Clubhouse Contracts pay modest amounts.

pros: Cheap way to become an MC President
Required to own the five MC drug and forgery businesses
Bar resupplies add a little background income
cons: Its own income streams are small
Mostly valuable only as a stepping stone
verdict: Buy the cheapest one only if you want MC businesses; on its own it is not a money maker.

name: Cocaine Lockup
income: Resupply-and-sell: buy or steal supplies, let staff process them into cocaine, then run sell missions.
description: The highest-value of the original MC drug businesses. Four locations are available, and Equipment and Staff upgrades raise production speed and product value.

earnings.perHourNote: Middle of guide figures for a fully upgraded lockup selling far ($46K-$90K/hr net); un-upgraded it earns far less.

pros: Highest-paying MC business
Produces while you do other things
Feeds goods into the Nightclub warehouse
cons: Needs costly staff and equipment upgrades to pay well
Larger sales can need several vehicles, which is hard alone
Supplies must be bought or stolen regularly
verdict: The only MC business most guides still recommend; worth it once upgraded, especially if you also own a Nightclub.

name: Methamphetamine Lab
income: Resupply-and-sell: supplies are cooked into meth over time and then delivered to buyers.
description: An MC business producing meth, offered at four locations. It is one of the more profitable MC businesses once fully upgraded.

earnings.perHourNote: Middle of guide figures for a fully upgraded lab ($28K-$65K/hr net); sources disagree a lot.

pros: Second-best MC business by value
Runs in the background
Adds stock to a Nightclub warehouse
cons: Outclassed by the cheaper-to-run Acid Lab
Can lose money un-upgraded if you buy supplies
Multi-vehicle sales are awkward solo
verdict: Only worth it fully upgraded and paired with a Nightclub; newer businesses earn more for the effort.

name: Weed Farm
income: Resupply-and-sell: grow weed from supplies and sell the product; owning Smoke on the Water raises its value.
description: A grow operation for cannabis, available at four locations. It is cheaper than the other drug businesses but earns less per unit.

earnings.perHourNote: Sources disagree strongly (about $16K-$37K/hr when upgraded); this is the middle value.

pros: Cheapest MC drug business
Smoke on the Water raises its product value
Contributes Nightclub stock
cons: Low earnings even with upgrades
Smaller solo sale limits
verdict: A low earner; buy it mainly for Nightclub stock or completionism rather than direct profit.

name: Counterfeit Cash Factory
income: Resupply-and-sell: print fake bills from supplies and sell them; owning the Hands On Car Wash raises its value.
description: An MC business that prints counterfeit money, offered at four locations. Upgrades speed up printing and increase the value of each batch.

earnings.perHourNote: Middle of guide figures for a fully upgraded factory ($27K-$48K/hr net).

pros: Decent mid-range MC business
Hands On Car Wash ownership raises its value
Feeds Nightclub stock
cons: Can run at a loss un-upgraded with bought supplies
Earns far less than active work
verdict: Fine as a background earner once upgraded, but not a priority purchase.

name: Document Forgery Office
income: Resupply-and-sell: produce forged documents from supplies and sell them; the lowest-earning MC business.
description: The cheapest MC business, producing fake IDs and paperwork. Four locations are available.

earnings.perHourNote: Middle of guide figures ($12K-$30K/hr net when upgraded); widely called the weakest MC business.

pros: Cheapest MC business
Small solo-friendly sales
cons: Lowest earnings of any MC business
Can lose money un-upgraded on bought supplies
Long payback time
verdict: Skip it unless you are collecting every business; almost anything else is a better use of the money.

name: Bunker
income: Resupply-and-sell weapons manufacturing; staff can also be assigned to research that unlocks vehicle and weapon upgrades.
description: An underground arms factory available at eleven locations across the map. It also stores the Mobile Operations Center and unlocks weaponized vehicles.

earnings.perHourNote: Middle of guide estimates for a fully upgraded bunker on bought supplies (about $45K-$110K/hr); a full sale is about $1.05M selling far.

pros: Big full-stock sales
Produces in the background while you play
Research unlocks useful vehicle and weapon upgrades
Feeds the Nightclub warehouse
cons: Needs expensive upgrades to earn well
Full sales can need several vehicles, tough alone
Long wait to fill
verdict: A reliable semi-passive earner once upgraded and a strong partner for the Nightclub; worth owning for most players.

name: Mobile Operations Center
income: No direct income; it houses vehicle and weapon workshops and is used for Gunrunning-related missions.
description: A mobile command trailer hauled by a truck cab. It can be fitted with a vehicle workshop, weapon workshop and command center, and lives inside the Bunker.
pros: Mobile weapon and vehicle workshop
Used for some Gunrunning content
cons: Earns no money
Expensive for what it adds

name: Hangar
income: Air Freight Cargo: source smuggled goods by air and sell them in bulk; Higgins Helitours raises its value.
description: An aircraft hangar at LSIA or Fort Zancudo that stores personal aircraft and runs the Air Freight smuggling business. It is also where the Avenger's Operations Terminal is fitted.

earnings.perHourNote: Guides disagree: about $360K/hr for fast land sourcing at $30K a crate, up to $500K-$700K/hr when rotating cargo types; this is the middle value and assumes a fast aircraft or Oppressor Mk II.

pros: Crate values were tripled in 2022, making it one of the best active businesses
Full 50-crate sales of top cargo pay over $2.4M
Higgins Helitours adds a 10% bonus
Sourcing works solo
cons: Solo sourcing brings in one crate at a time
Air sourcing missions are slow; good rates rely on a fast vehicle
Large sales in busy lobbies are risky
verdict: Underrated and very profitable for the price if you grind land sourcing with a fast vehicle; one of the best active buys.

name: Facility
income: No passive income; it hosts The Doomsday Heist and can be fitted with an Orbital Cannon and other upgrades.
description: A Cold War-era underground base used to plan The Doomsday Heist. Nine locations exist, mostly in Blaine County.

earnings.perHourNote: No reliable hourly figure; its income comes from The Doomsday Heist, which needs a crew.

pros: Hosts The Doomsday Heist
First weekly completion of classic heists now gets a large bonus
Orbital Cannon and other upgrades
cons: Doomsday needs two to four players
No passive income
Heist payouts were reduced in July 2026
verdict: Only worth it for players with a regular heist crew; solo players get little money from it.

name: Avenger
income: No direct income; with the Operations Terminal upgrade it starts Project Overthrow and other Los Santos Angels jobs.
description: A VTOL cargo aircraft that doubles as a flying base with optional workshops. A Facility used to be required, but since 2023 it can be bought without one and stored in a Hangar.

earnings.perHourNote: No reliable current hourly figure; LSA Operations reportedly pay around $45K-$70K plus a bonus, and recent payout changes lowered solo rewards.

pros: Operations Terminal unlocks repeatable missions that can be done solo
Also works as a mobile workshop and flying base
cons: Very expensive once the terminal is added
Mission payouts are modest
No passive income
verdict: A fun toy, but too expensive to buy purely for money.

name: Nightclub
income: Passive: a safe fills based on club popularity, and technicians in the basement warehouse accumulate goods from your other businesses for sale.
description: A club with resident DJs and a multi-level basement warehouse. It is considered one of the best passive earners because it needs no resupplying.

earnings.perHourNote: Safe only: $50K per in-game day (48 minutes) at full popularity, a figure most guides agree on. Warehouse goods from linked businesses add more on top.

pros: Best passive earner in the game
Warehouse turns your other businesses into extra stock with no supplies needed
Big warehouse sales fit in one delivery vehicle
Very low effort
cons: Popularity drops over time and must be topped up
Warehouse income depends on owning other businesses
Earns only while you are in a session
verdict: A must-own for almost everyone: cheap upkeep, real passive income, and it boosts the value of every other business you own.

name: Terrorbyte
requires: Own a Nightclub or the Garment Factory
income: No direct income; it unlocks Client Jobs and can be upgraded with a drone station and specialized workshop.
description: A mobile command truck with computer and drone facilities. It parks in the Nightclub or Garment Factory and is often used to manage businesses remotely.

earnings.perHourNote: No hourly figure; Client Jobs pay roughly $30K-$35K each.

pros: Client Jobs are easy to solo
Can be fitted with a drone and specialized workshop
cons: Low payouts per job
Expensive for the income it unlocks
verdict: Not worth buying for money alone; consider it only if you want its upgrades or utility.

name: Arena Workshop
income: No direct income; it converts vehicles into Arena War variants and stores them.
description: A workshop beneath the Maze Bank Arena where mechanic Sacha Yetarian builds arena vehicles. It connects to a garage with optional extra floors.
pros: Builds Arena War vehicles
Extra vehicle storage
cons: Earns no money
Arena War modes have small lobbies today

name: Casino Penthouse
income: No passive income; it unlocks Casino Work missions from Agatha Baker and a free daily casino perks set.
description: A luxury suite atop The Diamond Casino & Resort, available in several themed packages. Options include a party area, bar, spa and private dealer.

earnings.perHourNote: No reliable hourly figure for Casino Work; it is not a regular grind.

pros: Unlocks Casino Work missions
Daily casino perks
Luxury interior
cons: Very small earnings for the price
Most of the cost is cosmetic
verdict: Buy it for style or casino perks, not as an investment.

name: Arcade
income: A small passive safe that grows with the number of arcade cabinets installed; also the hub for The Diamond Casino Heist.
description: A retro arcade front with Lester's planning room in the basement. Six locations are available, and owners can play the games they install.

earnings.perHourNote: Arcade safe makes up to $5K per in-game day (about $6,250/hr); its real value is The Diamond Casino Heist, which has no reliable hourly figure after the July 2026 changes.

pros: Hosts The Diamond Casino Heist, still one of the biggest crew paydays
Small passive safe from arcade machines
First weekly heist completion carries a large bonus
cons: The heist needs at least two players
Repeat runs in the same week pay less after the 2026 changes
Safe income is tiny
verdict: Worth it if you have a crew for the Casino Heist; solo players should prioritize other properties.

name: Kosatka
requires: Meet Miguel Madrazo at The Music Locker
income: No passive income; it is the base for The Cayo Perico Heist, and its sonar helps find Hidden Caches.
description: A massive submarine HQ with a planning screen, moon pool and optional missile and helicopter upgrades. It can be called to various points around the coast.

earnings.perHourNote: Middle of guide figures that count the solo cooldown (about $90K-$340K/hr); estimates ignoring cooldowns run over $1M/hr. The July 2026 update made the lower-value Tequila primary far more common.

pros: Hosts The Cayo Perico Heist, still a top solo payday
Fully soloable
Pays back in only a few runs
Sonar helps find hidden caches
cons: July 2026 nerf cut the best primary targets and lowered average payouts
Long solo cooldown between runs
Repeat setups carry a fee
verdict: Still one of the strongest purchases for solo players even after the 2026 nerf; fill the cooldown with other businesses.

name: Auto Shop
income: Robbery Contracts for KDJ and Sessanta, plus modifying and delivering customer cars brought in by staff.
description: A tuner garage with a contract planning board and customer service bays. Five locations exist, and an LS Car Meet membership is often bought alongside it.

earnings.perHourNote: Middle of guide figures ($300K-$400K/hr) for back-to-back Robbery Contracts; contracts net about $153K-$166K each and the Union Depository about $270K solo.

pros: Among the best hourly rates for solo players
All contracts can be done alone
Exotic Exports and customer cars add extra cash
Pays back quickly
cons: Requires active play every session
Contract cut and setup costs reduce the take
Customer car deliveries pay little
verdict: One of the best buys in the game for solo players: cheap, fast payback, and consistently high hourly income.

name: LS Car Meet Membership
buyFrom: LS Car Meet (in person) or with an Auto Shop
income: No income; it unlocks Car Meet reputation rewards, the test track and tuner-related content.
description: Membership to the underground car meet in Cypress Flats. Members earn reputation levels that unlock discounts, clothing and car modifications.
pros: Very cheap
Unlocks Car Meet rewards, test track and tuner content
cons: Earns no money directly

name: Agency
income: Security Contracts, Payphone Hits and the Dr. Dre VIP Contract, plus a passive safe that pays more as contracts are completed.
description: Franklin Clinton's celebrity solutions firm, co-owned with the player. Four locations are available, and it includes Record A Studios access.

earnings.perHourNote: Middle of guide estimates (about $180K-$400K/hr) depending on the mix of Dr. Dre replays (about $900K each, $1.1M first weekly), Payphone Hits and Security Contracts; the safe adds up to $20K per in-game day.

pros: Dr. Dre contract pays close to $1M per run
Payphone Hits are quick and lucrative
Passive safe grows as you complete contracts
Everything can be done solo
cons: Safe needs many contracts before it pays well
Dre contract has a cooldown between replays
More expensive than most businesses
verdict: A top-tier purchase: several strong solo income streams in one property, and it pays itself back quickly.

name: Acid Lab (Brickade 6x6)
buyFrom: Warstock Cache & Carry (or unlocked through First Dose)
requires: Complete First Dose (then pay Mutt $750,000 to convert it) or buy it outright
income: Resupply-and-sell: supplies are turned into acid and sold; an equipment upgrade unlocked by Fooligan Jobs boosts output.
description: A Brickade 6x6 truck converted into a mobile drug lab. It is one of the few businesses that can be run without being a CEO or MC President.

earnings.perHourNote: Guides vary widely ($36K-$150K/hr) depending on supply costs and the Equipment Upgrade; about $80K/hr is the middle for an upgraded lab, with full batches around $335K.

pros: Best solo resupply-and-sell business
Every sale fits on one bike, so no multi-vehicle sells
Produces while you do other things
Cheap to resupply
cons: Needs the Equipment Upgrade (unlocked via Fooligan Jobs) to earn well
Smaller stock cap than the Bunker
Must be resupplied regularly
verdict: An easy recommendation for solo players: steady background income with painless single-vehicle sales.

name: Eclipse Blvd Garage
income: No income; it is large-capacity personal vehicle storage.
description: A multi-floor garage on Eclipse Boulevard designed to hold dozens of personal vehicles. It was added in the continuation of Los Santos Drug Wars.
pros: Huge vehicle storage capacity
cons: Earns no money
Expensive for storage alone

name: Salvage Yard
income: Vehicle robberies whose cars are sold or salvaged, tow truck jobs, and a passive safe.
description: A chop shop business that plans the weekly vehicle robberies. Five locations exist, from Paleto Bay to La Puerta.

earnings.perHourNote: Middle of guide figures ($117K-$700K/hr; most cluster around $200K-$390K) while running robberies, which pay about $240K-$410K each but are limited to three per week; tow jobs and the safe add up to about $24K per in-game day.

pros: Robberies pay very well and are fully soloable
Tow truck work and the safe add passive income
Fast payback
cons: Only three robberies are available each week
A tow truck must be bought separately
Safe rate falls if you stop towing
verdict: A strong buy for regular players thanks to big weekly robbery payouts plus a little passive income.

name: Bail Office
income: Active bounty hunting (standard and Most Wanted targets) plus passive income from hired agents who fill a safe.
description: Maude Eccles' bail enforcement business, available at five locations. Hired agents speed up bounty processing and earn money while the player is away.

earnings.perHourNote: Mainly one detailed guide estimate (about $140K-$150K/hr for a bounty session); hired agents add only about $12K-$15K/hr.

pros: Most Wanted targets pay well once per day
Hired agents earn small semi-passive cash
Varied, quick missions
cons: Standard bounties pay modestly and refresh slowly
Agents are expensive and take very long to pay back
Dead targets pay much less
verdict: Fun variety with okay money, but other businesses pay more per hour; buy it after the essentials.

name: Darnell Bros Garment Factory
income: The FIB Files mini-heists for Jodi Marshall plus a small passive office safe.
description: An old clothing factory converted into an operations base. The price includes a garage, a Terrorbyte bay and an MK II weapon workshop.

earnings.perHourNote: No consistent hourly figure; FIB File finales pay about $150K, the weekly Priority File about $300K, and the safe only $1.5K-$2K per in-game day.

pros: FIB Files pay well and can be done solo
Weekly Priority File gives a bigger payday
Small passive office safe
cons: Passive safe is tiny
Pricey for a single mission strand
verdict: Worth it for the FIB Files rather than the safe; a good mid-priority purchase for active players.

name: McKenzie Field Hangar
income: Arms Trafficking: source goods and deliver them in sell missions; also unlocks Oscar Guzman's mission strand.
description: A rural airfield hangar in Grapeseed run with Oscar Guzman. It adds extra aircraft storage on top of a personal hangar.

earnings.perHourNote: One detailed guide puts The Titan Job at about $240K-$275K/hr on Normal (more on Hard or the first weekly run); no reliable figure was found for Arms Trafficking.

pros: Unlocks The Titan Job, a strong solo heist with a weekly first-run bonus
Arms Trafficking adds extra missions
Relatively cheap
cons: Titan Job takes about an hour per run
Arms Trafficking payouts are not well documented
verdict: Good value for solo players thanks to The Titan Job; pays itself back in a handful of runs.

name: Hands On Car Wash
income: Launders dirty money for a passive safe that grows with the number of other businesses owned; raises Counterfeit Cash value.
description: A Strawberry car wash that serves as a money laundering front for Martin Madrazo's associates. It must be bought before the other Money Fronts businesses.

earnings.perHourNote: Sources conflict: safe estimates range from about $1.5K to $30K per in-game day depending on progress and owned businesses, so no single hourly figure is given.

pros: Safe grows with the number of businesses you own
Laundering missions are solo-friendly
Boosts Counterfeit Cash value
Unlocks the other Money Fronts
cons: Heat must be kept low or income stops
Safe cap is small
Full value needs lots of other businesses
verdict: A sensible pick for players who already own many businesses; less useful for newcomers.

name: Higgins Helitours
requires: Own the Hands On Car Wash
income: A laundering front that boosts Air Freight Cargo value and lets owners spawn helicopters there.
description: A helicopter tour company at the Vespucci helipad. Buying it includes a Higgins-branded Maverick.

earnings.perHourNote: No reliable hourly figure; its main value is a 10% bonus to Hangar Air Freight Cargo.

pros: 10% boost to Hangar cargo value
Handy helicopter spawn point
cons: Requires owning the Car Wash first
Only pays off if you sell a lot of Hangar cargo
verdict: Worth it only for regular Hangar sellers; everyone else can skip it.

name: Smoke on the Water
requires: Own the Hands On Car Wash
income: A laundering front that boosts Weed Farm product value and offers daily product pickups for cash and RP.
description: A legal weed dispensary in La Puerta near Vespucci Beach. It ties the Money Fronts system to the MC Weed Farm.

earnings.perHourNote: No reliable hourly figure; it mainly boosts Weed Farm value and offers small daily pickups.

pros: Raises Weed Farm product value
Daily product pickups give cash and RP
cons: The Weed Farm it boosts is a weak earner
Small direct income
verdict: Low priority; only for Weed Farm owners or Money Fronts completionists.

name: Mansion
income: No direct income; an AI concierge can boost a business's production, mansion security reduces raids, and it hosts Michael's mission and The Kortz Center Heist.
description: The most expensive homes in GTA Online: the Tongva Estate, the Vinewood Residence and the Richman Villa. Prices quoted are the commonly listed figures, which some sources say include a discount for completing earlier New Listing missions.

earnings.perHourNote: No direct income; the AI concierge production boost and The Kortz Center Heist (which also needs the Art Studio) are where its value lies.

pros: AI concierge can speed up a business
Security reduces raids
Required for the Art Studio and The Kortz Center Heist
cons: Extremely expensive
Earns nothing directly
Very long payback even with the heist
verdict: A luxury purchase; only worth it for wealthy players who also want The Kortz Center Heist.

name: Art Studio (Mansion upgrade)
income: No passive income; it is required to host The Kortz Center Heist.
description: A studio added to a Mansion where counterfeiter Yong-Rae forges replica paintings. It serves as the planning hub for the Kortz Center Heist.

earnings.perHourNote: No fixed hourly figure; The Kortz Center Heist pays roughly $2M on the first weekly solo completion and about $300K-$480K on repeat runs that week.

pros: Hosts The Kortz Center Heist, with a large first weekly payout
Mostly soloable
cons: Requires a Mansion, so the full setup costs around $16M
Repeat runs pay far less
Takes many weeks to break even
verdict: Good weekly money once you own a Mansion, but the total entry cost is so high that it is a late-game buy.

name: High-End Apartment
income: No income; it includes the Heist Planning Room needed to host the original heists.
description: Top-tier city apartments with a 10-car garage. They are the cheapest way to host the original 2015 heists.
pros: Heist Planning Room for the original heists
Cheap at the low end
cons: Earns no money by itself
Original heists need a full crew

name: Stilt House
income: No income; it counts as a high-end property with a heist planning room.
description: Hillside homes in the Vinewood Hills perched on stilts, each with a 10-car garage. Prices vary by address.
pros: Counts as a high-end property with a heist room
Unique hillside views
cons: Earns no money

name: Executive Custom Apartment
income: No income; it offers selectable interior styles and a heist planning room.
description: Penthouse-style apartments whose interior style can be chosen and changed. The most expensive is Eclipse Towers Penthouse Suite 3.
pros: Choice of interior styles
Heist planning room
cons: Earns no money
Costs more than a standard high-end apartment

name: Galaxy Super Yacht
income: No passive income; later updates added Yacht Missions playable from it.
description: A huge private yacht in three models (Orion, Pisces and Aquarius) that can be moored at locations around the coast. It includes a helipad and a hot tub.

earnings.perHourNote: No reliable hourly figure for Yacht Missions.

pros: Yacht Missions add some playable content
Prestige and a mobile spawn point
cons: Very expensive
Mission payouts are small for the price
verdict: A status symbol rather than an investment; do not buy it to make money.
